d: The pouch of Douglas: the peritoneal recess between the uterus and the rectum, lying on the posterior vaginal fornix. It is the lowest point of the female peritoneal cavity, where fluid collects first.
The suspensory ligament of the ovary: a peritoneal fold from the ovary to the pelvic side wall that carries the ovarian artery and vein. The ureter lies just medial to it at the pelvic brim.

The connective tissue between the parietal fascia of the pelvic walls and the visceral fascia of the organs. Its condensations, the cardinal, uterosacral and pubocervical ligaments, support the cervix and upper vagina.
The distance from the sacral promontory to the lower edge of the pubic symphysis, measured on vaginal exam. Subtracting 1.5 to 2 cm estimates the obstetric conjugate, the true inlet diameter.

Parasympathetic nerves from the S2 to S4 ventral rami that join the inferior hypogastric plexus. They contract the detrusor, produce erection and drive the hindgut, unlike every other splanchnic nerve, which is sympathetic.

A midline elevation on the posterior wall of the prostatic urethra, also called the verumontanum. The small blind prostatic utricle opens at its center, and the two ejaculatory ducts open on either side of it.

A network of valveless veins around the vertebral column that connects with the pelvic, prostatic and breast veins. Flow reverses when abdominal pressure rises, so tumor cells from the prostate, breast or uterus can reach the spine without passing through the lungs.

Semen flowing backward into the bladder at orgasm because the internal urethral sphincter fails to close. It gives a dry orgasm and cloudy urine afterward, and follows sympathetic nerve injury, bladder neck surgery or alpha-1 blockers.
